beta adrenergically mediated adenylate cyclases are present in rat cerebral capillary fractions and that the receptors are mixed in character.
beta adrenergically mediated activation of adenyl cyclase occurs in cerebral microvessels, and that the beta receptors are heterogeneous.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of beta-adrenergic agonist drugs on the adenylate cyclases of the rat brain.
the role of the beta adrenerigc receptor in the control of adenylate clycylase activity in rat cerebral capillary preparations.
the effects of the beta-adrenergic agonist isoproterenon (IPN) on the permeability of the blood-brain barrier.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the beta adrenerigic receptor in the cerebral capillary is a beta2 receptor, but that the receptor is not a pure beta2 receptor.

the beta adrenerigic agonist-induced activation of adenylcate cyclase in cerebral capillaries involves a population of beta1 and beta2 receptors which are sensitive to blockade by beta adrenergics and propranolol, and that the beta1 and beta 2 receptors may be present in different proportions in capillaries from different brain regions.
the beta adreneric receptors in the capillaries of the cerebral cortex are of the beta1 and beta2 types, and that the beta2 subtype is predominant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the capillary beta1 and beta2 receptors are not homogeneous and are differentially sensitive to the agonists and antagonists tested.
the beta adrenerigic receptor system of the cerebral microvasculature is a complex one and is capable of mediating a variety of physiological responses.
the beta adrenergeic receptors in rat cerebral microvessels are of the beta1 and beta2 subtypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beta receptors are present in the capillaries of the cerebral cortex.
capillaries are a target for beta agonists and antagonists.
the cerebral microvessels are not a passive structure but are actively involved in the regulation of cerebral vascular resistance and cerebral blood flow.
